spec.description: Is Home-IDS working, what reached you, and how every device looks right now.

options.content: **Start here.** Top row: is everything running. Second row: what the system did in the last 24 hours. Then the **Master Threat Ledger**, with one row per device. Hover any tile or column header for an explanation. The other dashboards go deeper: **2** Threat Landscape, **3** Device Deep Dive, **4** Autonomy & Learning, **5** System Health & Operations.
Green means running. A red tile means that part is down; the other layers keep working on their own.

spec.title: Detection engine
spec.description: Is Prometheus reaching the Home-IDS engine? If this is down, every other number here is stale.

spec.expr: max(up{job="home_ids"})

spec.title: Job scheduler
spec.description: Is the scheduler daemon (which runs the LLM review, retro-hunt, pruning, autotune...) reachable?

spec.expr: max(up{job="home_ids_scheduler"})

spec.title: Host load
spec.description: The health manager's view of the machine: Normal, Resource pressure, Conserving (non-essential work paused) or Critical.

spec.expr: home_ids_health_pressure_level

spec.title: Parts needing attention
spec.description: How many internal components the health manager does not rate Healthy (retired ones excluded). 0 is normal; see dashboard 5 for which.

spec.expr: count(home_ids_health_component_state > 0) or vector(0)

spec.title: Network sensor (Zeek)
spec.description: Is Zeek's traffic log being read? Without it, scans, TLS fingerprints and lateral movement go unseen.

spec.expr: home_ids_zeek_status

spec.title: DNS blocking (Pi-hole)
spec.description: Can Home-IDS reach Pi-hole to block domains?

spec.expr: home_ids_ips_pihole_status

spec.title: Router isolation
spec.description: Can Home-IDS cut a device off at the router?

spec.expr: home_ids_ips_router_status

spec.title: LAN tarpit
spec.description: Is the local ARP/NDP tarpit (traps a device on the LAN) armed?

spec.expr: home_ids_ips_tarpit_status

options.content: Counted from the evidence graph, so these survive restarts.

spec.title: Alerts sent to you
spec.description: Alerts that passed every gate (HIGH or CRITICAL, not hidden as a false positive) in the last 24h. Low is normal.

spec.expr: sum(home_ids_argus_alert_events_24h{status="FIRED"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: Hidden as false positives
spec.description: Alerts the false-positive filter suppressed in the last 24h (typically trusted destinations). Nothing is deleted; they stay in the log.

spec.expr: sum(home_ids_argus_alert_events_24h{status="SUPPRESSED_AUTONOMOUS"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: Logged below the alert bar
spec.description: Candidates recorded for context but not strong enough to alert on.

spec.expr: sum(home_ids_argus_alert_events_24h{status="LOGGED_ONLY"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: High / critical decisions
spec.description: Decisions the engine rated High or Critical in the last 24h (before incident grouping and false-positive filtering).

spec.expr: sum(home_ids_argus_decisions_24h{state=~"HIGH|CRITICAL"}) or vector(0)

spec.title: Active incidents
spec.description: Distinct incidents (a device + what it is doing, grouped) with activity in the last 24h.

spec.expr: home_ids_argus_incidents_active_24h

spec.title: Devices isolated now
spec.description: Devices cut off right now by the router and/or the LAN tarpit. 0 is normal.

spec.expr: count(max by (device) (home_ids_ips_tarpit_active == 1 or home_ids_ips_router_isolated_active == 1)) or vector(0)

spec.title: Domains blocked now
spec.description: Domains currently blocked in Pi-hole on Home-IDS's instruction.

spec.expr: count(home_ids_ips_active_blocks == 1) or vector(0)

options.content: One row per device, one column per signal. **Read left to right:** the verdict, why it was reached, how well it is backed up, then the individual signals. Hover a column header for what it means. Click a device name to open its deep dive. Filter with the **device** box at the top.

properties.value: The device's name as the engine knows it. Click to open its deep dive.
The engine's current decision for this device. High and Critical can trigger automatic containment.
Which rule or hypothesis path produced the verdict.
How sure the engine is of its verdict (not how dangerous the device is).
How many independent kinds of evidence back the verdict. HIGH needs at least 2.
How many different evidence families were seen (DNS, network behaviour, reputation...).
Reputation of the destination behind the current evidence: own network, trusted, known infrastructure, unknown, weak bad signal, confirmed bad.
Alerts about this device that reached you in the last 24h.
Alerts about this device the false-positive filter hid in the last 24h.
Which attack stage this device's traffic most resembles (suspected, not confirmed).
How unusual the device looks to its own anomaly model (0 = normal for it).
How many times the baseline detected a lasting change in this device's behaviour and re-learned it.
How much the false-positive filter has learned to trust this device's usual behaviour (0-100%).
Automatic sensitivity shift. Below 0: stricter after confirmed threats (floor -1.5). Above 0: more lenient after corrected false positives.
How many thresholds autotune has calibrated specifically for this device (others use its device-type or global value).
AbuseIPDB community reports for this device's destinations.
VirusTotal detections for this device's destinations.
Connections whose TLS fingerprint (JA4) matches known malware.
Contacts to a configured decoy address. Any hit is a strong sign of scanning.
Unanswered or rejected connection attempts, typical of port scanning.
Connections to DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers that skip your Pi-hole.
Bytes this device sent out in the current window.
Is this device cut off right now (router and/or LAN tarpit)?
Still learning what is normal for this device (new or recently reset), or monitored normally.
Learning is paused while the device looks risky, so an attacker can't teach the baseline that bad is normal.
Exempted from containment by your configuration.
Device type as inferred or configured.

spec.title: Alert outcomes (rolling 24 h)
spec.description: For each moment, how many alerts in the preceding 24 hours were sent to you, hidden as false positives, or only logged.

spec.expr: sum by (status) (home_ids_argus_alert_events_24h)

spec.title: Decision paths (per minute)
spec.description: How the engine reached its decisions over time. A mix shifting towards corroborated paths means sharper detection.

spec.expr: sum by (path) (rate(home_ids_decision_path_total[5m])) * 60

options.content: Raw alert records from the log stream (Loki). Every number above comes from Prometheus; this table exists because a metrics store can't hold log lines.

spec.title: Alerts that reached you
spec.description: HIGH or CRITICAL alerts that the false-positive filter did not hide, newest first. Expand a row for the full evidence.

spec.expr: {job="home_ids_alerts"} | json | type="ids_alert" | suppressed!="true" | hee_decision_path=~"hard_stop|hypothesis_high|tier5_confirmed|tier5_corroborated|geofence_uncorroborated|suricata_uncorroborated" | json device="device.hostname", signature="signature", risk="risk", why="hee_decision_path"
